court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
case_name: A.Revathi vs The Inspector General Of Registration

parties.respondent_defendant: The Inspector General Of Registration, R.Jagadeesan (Respondents)

facts_of_case: Petitioner's neighbour, R.Jagadeesan, allegedly forced her to register a marriage certificate. Petitioner claims no such marriage was solemnized.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage conducted in secrecy with few strangers around will not amount to solemnization, as required under Section 7 and 7-A of the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: The Division Bench observed that a marriage performed in secrecy in the chambers of Advocates and Bar Association Rooms will not amount to solemnisation.
cited_cases: S.Balakrishnan Pandiyan and another v. The Superintendent of Police, Kanchipuram, (2014) 6 CTC 129

legal_principles.principle: No registration of marriage can be done under the Tamil Nadu Registration of Marriages Act, 2009 without the physical presence of the parties to the marriage before the Registrar, except under special circumstances after recording the reasons.
legal_principles.held: The Division Bench disposed of those Habeas Corpus Petitions in the following manner: (b) No registration of marriage can be done under the Tamil Nadu Registration of Marriages Act, 2009 without the physical presence of the parties to the marriage before the Registrar, except under special circumstances after recording the reasons.
applicable_acts_sections: Tamil Nadu Registration of Marriages Act — Section X
cited_cases: S.Balakrishnan Pandiyan and another v. The Superintendent of Police, Kanchipuram, (2014) 6 CTC 129

outcome.final_order: The communication sought to be quashed is illegal and the second respondent is directed to delete, cancel and remove the said certificate of marriage from his records.

use_for_drafting: drafting a writ petition under Article 226
